::: {#exm-acceptance-ratio}
#### Acceptance ratio for a Bernoulli posterior

With $r = 55$ successes in $n = 91$ trials, a uniform prior,
and the [symmetric](#def-symmetric-proposal) proposal of @exm-proposal-distribution,
the $q$ terms cancel and the prior is constant,
so moving from $\pi^{(t)} = 0.5$ to $\pi^* = 0.6$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha
&= \frac{0.6^{55}\, 0.4^{36}}{0.5^{55}\, 0.5^{36}}
&& \text{(Bernoulli likelihood ratio)}\\
&= 1.2^{55}\, 0.8^{36}
&& \text{(combine the powers)}\\
&\approx 7.35
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The reverse move, from $0.6$ to $0.5$, has $\alpha \approx 1/7.35 \approx 0.136$.
:::
